findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: In `EventManager.create()`, the code destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then immediately accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. When an event has Google Meet (`MeetLocationType`) as its location but no destination calendar (empty array or null — which this PR now produces in many places, e.g. handleNewBooking sets `null` and other handlers set `[]`), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and reading `.integration` throws a TypeError, breaking booking creation. The previous code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which was safe. This needs `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Team destination calendars silently dropped when organizer/event type has no destination calendar
findings.body: For collective events, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, and later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op on `null`. So if the main host has no destination calendar but other collective hosts do, those hosts' calendars are never added and they won't get calendar events — the exact scenario this PR is meant to fix. The code should initialize an array first (e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` before pushing, or use `(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []).concat(teamDestinationCalendars)`).

findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback find() can never match, producing undefined calendarId
findings.body: In both `updateEvent` (line ~254-256) and `deleteEvent` (line ~315-317), the fallback branch is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. This branch is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined), so `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` can never be true and the expression always evaluates to `undefined`. Previously the fallback used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, which resolved to the destination calendar. Now, when `updateEvent`/`deleteEvent` are called without an explicit external calendar id, `calendarId` becomes `undefined` (update) and the Google API call will fail or target the wrong calendar. The fallback should use the first destination calendar's externalId instead.

findings.title: Recurring-event cancellation deletes are re-executed once per calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring-event deletion block (`if (bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings)`) iterates over all of the user's calendar credentials and all updated bookings. This PR wrapped that block inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`, so with multiple calendar references (now normal for multi-host collective bookings) the same full sweep of deletes runs once per reference — deleting the same events N times and pushing duplicate promises into `apiDeletes`. The recurring-cancellation sweep should be hoisted out of the per-reference loop (or guarded to run only once).

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses possibly undefined calendarId
findings.body: In `createEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is computed via `destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and falls back to `"primary"` only for the `events.insert` call. The follow-up `calendar.events.patch` that writes the hangout link description uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly, without the `"primary"` fallback. When no destination calendar matches the credential, the insert succeeds on the primary calendar but the patch is sent with `calendarId: undefined`, so the description update fails silently.
